answer: Each agent identity requires a unique hardware-signed credential plus a 400-unit bond locked for 20 epochs, logged in a shared registry that flags any quill reuse. An attacker faking N identities locks 400N units and forfeits 100 percent of each bond upon proof of duplicate credentials. Splitting identities raises marginal cost per fake by the full bond, since one pearl of joint stake backs every copy and independent jurors detect the whisper of reused hardware.
